text:
tanya: heads up — started rolling the new rate policy canary at 10:00 PDT to 5% of traffic, noticed a small spike in auth-errors and unexpected quota hits. anyone else see this?
sam: saw it. alerting showed 401s from the auth service + 429s in the proxy. odd combo.
lia: tickets coming in from a couple of customers complaining about sudden failures during bursty traffic. no billing anomalies yet.
jordan-oncall: I’m on it. can you paste a sample request id or logs?
tanya: request ids: req_5f8a12b3 from edge-17 and req_5f8a8d22 from edge-22. logs show: 
```
ERROR token-validator: token expired=false, malformed=false, missing_scopes=false, quota_status=EXHAUSTED
auth-service: 401 invalid_token for user=acct-1234 (header x-api-key missing?)
proxy: 429 route=/v1/generate reason=rate_limit_policy_canary
```
sam: weird — token-validator saying not expired yet auth-service logs say missing header. might be a header rewrite bug in the canary proxy.
lia: repro steps from support: 
1) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "X-Client-Id: acct-1234" -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
2) quickly fire 50 concurrent requests
result: about 5% return 401, ~30% return 429, rest succeed
jordan-oncall: can you reproduce locally against the canary endpoint? tanya, which hosts are in canary?
tanya: canary nodes: edge-17, edge-22, edge-37. routing policy sends new sessions to these for 5% sample.
sam: i pushed a log patch to show full request headers on the canary only: run id 1729543245. check S3 logs.
deploy-bot: deploy canary-ratepolicy v2 -> 3 nodes (edge-17, edge-22, edge-37) at 2024-10-03T17:00:12Z
lia: customers are low-impact for now but support thread #CS-578 has a dev complaining they can’t complete a build step; asking for ETA.
jordan-oncall: priority: investigate header rewrite. if canary is dropping X-Client-Id or Authorization when proxying to auth-service, that explains both 401 and quota attribution mismatches.
tanya: confirmed header rewrite rule was added to the new filter: 
```
# canary filter snippet
remove_headers: ["X-Forwarded-For"]
# accidentally removed :authority and X-Client-Id when normalizing
```
I see an edge rule that normalizes pseudo-headers incorrectly.
sam: ok that’s actionable. mitigation path: 1) roll the canary back 2) patch filter to preserve auth and client-id headers, 3) re-run canary at 1% with enhanced observability
lia: can we do a targeted rollback only for edge-22? most 401s trace to edge-22 in the last 15min.
jordan-oncall: yes — we can remove edge-22 from canary pool and leave the others. that should reduce customer impact while we patch. @tanya can you coordinate?
tanya: removing edge-22 now. giving it ~30s to drain sessions.
deploy-bot: remove edge-22 from canary pool request accepted at 2024-10-03T17:05:11Z
sam: i’ll open a hotfix branch: preserve-headers-fix and build image with the filter change.
lia: support update posted: "We are investigating a subset of requests affected by the rate policy canary; temporary rollback in progress. Will update in 20m." :hourglass_flowing_sand: 
tanya: after removing edge-22, recent logs show 401s down to ~0.3% and 429s back to baseline.
jordan-oncall: great. plan: sam to build + test, tanya to stage patch on edge-22 locally, then staged canary to 1% with traffic shaping and payload-level tracing. lia will hold customer comms.
sam: hotfix PR opened: https://git.internal/r/redwood/canary-filters/pulls/412 — includes unit tests for header preservation.
tanya: once validated, let's do a controlled canary bump: 0.5% -> 1% -> 5% with heartbeat checks after each step; auto-rollback on >1% auth error regression.
jordan-oncall: agreed. also add metric: auth_header_present_count and client_id_tagged_count for the canary nodes.
lia: will update CS-578 and notify affected accounts with a note about transient routing issue and mitigation.
sam: CI build passed on hotfix, pushing image to staging for smoke tests.
deploy-bot: image push canary-fix:v20241003-5 completed at 2024-10-03T17:21:40Z
tanya: smoke tests pass on edge-22 in staging. scheduling staged canary now at 0.5% with stricter observability.
jordan-oncall: i’ll monitor SLO dashboards and set alert threshold to 0.5% auth_error_rate for the next hour.
lia: thanks all, nice triage — support will close the immediate tickets after customer follow-ups.
sam: follow-up items: postmortem note (who, what, fix, monitoring), update canary checklist to include header-preservation test, add a runbook snippet for partial-rollbacks.
tanya: logging note: avoid logging raw tokens in debug logs; use token mask.
jordan-oncall: closing loop — keep me posted. revert if anything spikes. :white_check_mark:
